patch_description:
The validation failure was caused by the recursive implementation corrupting row identity and column alignment. In particular, `column_recursion` writes completed futures to `result_df.loc[i]` in completion order rather than source-row order, and the later `original_index` merge/sort path can detach values from their original rows. The code also mutates the input with an `original_index` column, relies on attribute access for arbitrary column names, and returns an empty ordering list despite physically reordering cells.

This replacement keeps every input row and value, does not add helper columns, preserves the original index and shape, and returns a valid per-row column ordering. It evaluates a bounded set of deterministic prefix-oriented column-order candidates using the actual sorted-string LCP Trie objective, including a required global frequency ordering and a conditional grouping candidate when bounded work permits it.
